purpose: Select ordinary coding work independently of whether Gauntlet helps, then preserve enough state to rerun the comparison.
preferred_source: Fresh requests from the user's actual projects, captured before solving.
fallback_source: Existing real issue-resolution tasks with available source snapshots, runnable dependencies and validated checks; public benchmark tasks are an external reference, not proof of relevance to this user's work.
research_boundary: Reuse real-issue task construction and execution validation. The proposed small local sample and its funding gates are our choices, not a research-established effect size or sample-size justification.
initial_sequence: One bounded native-agent pilot on a fresh ordinary task to qualify setup, acceptance and accounting. Treat any task inspected while tuning the procedure as development data.

After selecting a distinct treatment and freezing its protocol, use the first four eligible requests from the agreed workload, in recorded arrival order, for an exploratory paired screen. Keep the candidate/rejection log.
If a useful difference appears, quote a separate confirmation on untouched tasks. Four tasks do not establish general superiority or equivalence.

example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.request_example: A validator accepts an invalid record; reject it without rejecting valid boundary cases.
example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.acceptance_example: Observed bad input fails before repair; correct behavior and valid edge cases pass afterward, with existing regressions checked.

example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.request_example: Add an export that respects the selected filters and preserves the existing output contract.
example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.acceptance_example: Inspect the generated file for selected records, escaping and empty results; verify compatibility for existing callers.

example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.request_example: Fix a guided tour that continues advancing after the user presses pause.
example_task_classes_not_selected_issues.acceptance_example: Run a frozen start/pause/resume sequence and observe state transitions; include a browser check when browser behavior is part of the claim.

eligibility: A genuine requested outcome in the predeclared workload; no planted defect required to make an orchestration mechanism fire.
Bounded scope and acceptance requirements understandable without the hidden solution.
Starting source, input data and dependencies can be preserved and restored in isolated workspaces.
A claimed bug is reproduced or a requested missing capability is demonstrated before solver work.
Independent acceptance checks distinguish at least plausible bad outputs from valid behavior; extra hidden requirements are prohibited.
Environment and grader preparation fit the quoted resources; otherwise log exclusion before model outcomes are seen.
exposure_policy: Use fresh sessions with the same frozen baseline configuration; do not pass prior solutions or the competing arm's transcript to a solver.
Preserve normal host tools and orchestration capabilities in the native control. Record memory and context policy for both arms.
Previously solved tasks and tasks used to tune prompts, checks or routing are development data, never untouched confirmation.
Public historical solutions may have been encountered during training or evaluation. Freshness reduces some exposure risks but does not prove absence of contamination.
Do not admit tasks because a Gauntlet critic rejected them. Mechanism diagnostics require a separately labeled conditional population.

required_packet_fields.task_id_and_origin: Stable ID, original request/issue and capture time; public reference or private local alias.
required_packet_fields.request: Exact request, supplied context, clarified requirements and non-goals frozen before the comparison.
required_packet_fields.starting_artifact: Commit plus any uncommitted patch, or a complete source snapshot; content hashes and retained files.
required_packet_fields.environment: OS/runtime/tool versions, dependency locks, setup commands and required services; preserve reproducible fixtures for volatile inputs.
required_packet_fields.inputs: Exact datasets/files/reference versions and initial state.
required_packet_fields.acceptance: Requirements, observable checks and regression cases authored independently of solver output; held-out evaluation content kept outside solver access.
required_packet_fields.agent_configuration: Host/client, model, effort, tools, permissions, memory/context, delegation and other workflow settings.
required_packet_fields.execution: Shared ceilings, planned order and repetition policy; count every started run, unsuccessful attempt and intervention.
required_packet_fields.exposure_and_selection: What was previously seen/solved, pilot versus screen versus confirmation, queue position and exclusion reasons.

reproducibility_boundary: Reproducible means restoring the task and evaluation conditions. It does not guarantee identical stochastic outputs; provider/model changes can limit exact reruns and must be reported.

historical_examples.limits: Tiny historical fix already solved by both arms; an earlier pilot exposed answer history. Source checkout is external to the public spec.

historical_examples.use: Ordinary feature and generated-build example only.
historical_examples.limits: Already solved by both arms; no held-out checks in the spec. External source and dependency packaging need verification; jsdom does not establish actual browser behavior.

full_cost_policy: Include task capture, environment preparation, grader validation, research, all agent attempts and active human time. Unmeasured categories remain null; reused material is not free research.
